kf: **Pemphigus vulgaris** is a rare autoimmune blistering disease with **flaccid blisters and erosions**, almost always involving the **mouth**.
Autoantibodies to **desmogleins 3 (± 1)** separate keratinocytes (acantholysis): **Nikolsky sign** positive.
Oral erosions often precede skin lesions by months; pemphigus foliaceus (Dsg1) spares the mucosa.
Extensive or unwell: **same-day admission**; mucosal only: urgent dermatology.
Specialist first line: **rituximab plus prednisolone**; untreated mortality is high.

sub: Adults 40–60; more common in Ashkenazi Jewish and Mediterranean, South Asian populations.

myths: **"Recurrent mouth ulcers are just aphthous"**: persistent oral erosions in an adult need biopsy.
patho_lead: Antibodies **cut the glue (desmosomes)** between epidermal cells, so the epidermis falls apart.

mech.t: Keratinocytes lose adhesion and separate just above the basal layer.
The thin roof ruptures easily, leaving painful erosions.
mech.cap: Pemphigus splits within the epidermis (flaccid blister); pemphigoid splits beneath it (tense blister).

mech.t: Which desmogleins are targeted explains mucosal versus skin involvement.

histo: Suprabasal acantholysis with 'tombstone' basal cells; DIF: intercellular IgG and C3 ('fishnet'); serum Dsg1/Dsg3 ELISA.

sub: Penicillamine, ACE inhibitors; paraneoplastic pemphigus with lymphoma causes severe stomatitis.

comp: Dehydration, malnutrition, sepsis, steroid side effects; death without treatment.
prog: Controlled in most with modern treatment; relapses occur.
